name: imram

attributes.attribute: an Old Irish word for voyage, the term for tale type in which a hero travels to the Otherworld
describe the hero's journey to the Otherworld and what he meets there, some with aisling or satiric elements

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Imram is an Irish literary term. The plural is imrama. It means voyage. Voyage tales tell how a hero travels to the Otherworld and what he meets there. Some have aspects of the aisling, or dream poem. A few contain elements of satire. Famous examples include the Voyage of Bran and the Voyage of Maelduin. In one a human is drawn from home by a fairy lover. In the other the hero meets frightening Otherworld women at sea. A related form is the adventure. It gives less weight to the journey and more to the goal.

okr.objective: Document imram, the Irish literary term for voyage tale.
key_results: Record imram, plural imrama, as the word for voyage.
Note the Voyage of Bran and Voyage of Maelduin as famous examples.
